industry.size: Indian retail ~Rs112 trn in FY26 (+~10%); organised retail ~Rs15 trn (+15%, ~13% of the total); e-retail ~Rs5.5 trn (+16%, ~4.9%); food and grocery ~32% of organised retail; retail to grow 9.7-10.4% a year over 2025-30 (CRISIL Research, cited in AR FY26 MD&A).
industry.dmartShare: ~1.5% of Indian retail; DMart's categories cover only ~50% of the retail wallet (Emkay initiation, 12-Apr-2026).
industry.quickCommerce: Quick commerce (Blinkit, Instamart, Zepto, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now) is already ~1.5x modern trade in key metros (Emkay estimate) and is moving into the next 50-100 cities. Emkay's monthly-basket check: QC prices only 4-13% above DMart stores before bank offers, similar or lower after them. Blinkit runs at 25-26% gross margin vs DMart's 14-15%; dark stores turn inventory ~10x faster per store than DMart's ~2x (Emkay). DMart management (28-Jul-2026): more players than last year; some small baskets move to QC for convenience and this 'is not going to change over the next few years'; FMCG vendors still doubling down on DMart, often its largest single customer.
industry.metroVsTier2: Older, dense metro stores (Mumbai, Bangalore) are near capacity; DMart opens nearby stores, cannibalising same-store growth. Tier 1-2 stores ramp better and grow faster (management, 28-Jul-2026). Emkay and Goldman Sachs: older large-metro stores flat y/y in Q1FY27.
industry.src: AR FY26; Emkay initiating coverage (12-Apr-2026, via Business Standard broker-tips PDF); analyst meet transcript (28-Jul-2026)

excluded.ABFRL: Loss-making in every year FY20-26 (FY26 net loss Rs830 cr) and restructured by the 2025 demerger of its lifestyle brands: no P/E history to compare.
excluded.SHOPERSTOP: Net profit Rs11 cr in FY25 and a loss in FY26: the trailing P/E (~258x at 30-Sep-2026) and its five-year history are meaningless.
excluded.VMM: Vishal Mega Mart listed in Dec-2024: under two years of P/E history, no five-year median. Shown as a sensitivity row only.

peers.note: Retail peer set for the consumer-services batch (set here, first retail report; TRENT matches it): DMART, TRENT, METROBRAND, BATAINDIA, PAGEIND, with ABFRL, SHOPERSTOP and VMM excluded as stated; each report excludes itself. Sector de-rating = median of the used peers' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep-2026 close vs their five-year (Oct-2021 to Sep-2026) median, Screener data. Caveats shown as sensitivity rows: Metro Brands listed Dec-2021 (4.8 years of history); Trent's and Bata's medians include 2021-22 points on depressed earnings, and Bata's FY26 profit fell 60% (FY25 had Rs188 cr of other income). Every sub-set gives -29.6% to -30.3%.

Foreign brokers' July-2026 targets (Citi, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Bernstein, Macquarie, Jefferies) appear only in search snippets that mix 2025 and 2026 notes; we leave them out (see gaps).
street.methodSummary: No single method: JM uses P/E (65x Mar-28E); HSIE, PL and Emkay use DCF but state the implied one-year-forward P/E (58x, ~65x, 54x); MOSL uses EV/EBITDA and states the implied P/E (~60x Sep-28E). P/E on one-year-forward EPS is the common language, so it is our primary method; EV/EBITDA and DCF are cross-checks.

stockEvents.event: Q4FY26 business update: revenue +19%, 58 stores added in the quarter; stock rose ~4%
First trading day after Q1FY27 results: stock fell ~4% to a low of Rs3,910 (Business Today)
Annual analyst meet: ~15% store-addition benchmark, SSSG to stay near ~8%, DMart Ready in 11 cities; MOSL downgraded to Neutral

moat.scale: Largest food-and-grocery hypermarket chain by revenue in India (Rs67,000 cr standalone) and often an FMCG vendor's largest single customer (management).
moat.cost: EDLC: owned stores (no rent escalation), fast vendor payment (7 days) for better terms, no-frills formats, cluster-based logistics; opex ~6.4% of revenue standalone (FY26: staff 2.0%, other 4.4%).
moat.weakness: Price advantage over QC is narrowing (Emkay basket check); narrow categories (~50% of the wallet); online business loss-making; dependence on land acquisition limits speed.

critiques: Bears (Emkay, PL): QC is taking the convenience basket in metros and narrowing DMart's price edge; SSSG stuck at 5-8%; ROE structurally lower at ~13% as capex outruns internal cash.
Bulls (MOSL in May, Elara): store additions can run at 85-90 a year; Tier 2-3 stores ramp well; margins have bottomed.
Middle (HSIE, MOSL after July): measured growth (~15% store additions) does not justify a re-rating; DCF / EV/EBITDA targets around Rs4,000-4,100.
governance: Founder-promoter (Damani family, 74.5%) with professional management; MD & CEO change in Feb-2026 (Noronha to Asawa) was planned a year ahead; independent chairman; EY-network auditor; tiny related-party flows; no pledge; no dividend ever.
gaps: Foreign brokers' post-Q1 targets (Citi, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Bernstein, Macquarie, Jefferies, Kotak) could not be tied to dated July-2026 notes; search snippets mixed 2025 and 2026 targets. Left out of the street table and median.
